title: [MIG-005] Ship supported library exports, CLI entry points and a versioned package artifact
objective: Create an installable package whose library API, types, CLI and runtime assets work outside the source tree.
inScope: Implement the agreed package identity and documented exports/types with a distribution file allowlist. Bundle compiled ESM, declarations, required schemas/templates and license/notices; make public subpaths explicit and reject unsupported deep imports.

Provide a Vibez standalone binary and a documented compatibility decision for the existing agent binary/commands, JSON envelope and exit codes. Preserve supported commands; describe reserved operations honestly until MIG-006 integrates #78. Standalone means a supported executable install, not a request to write a custom host script.

Add reproducible build/pack metadata, package-version lookup from the installation, content checksum/provenance, dependency declarations and release-candidate generation. Distinguish consumer runtime dependencies from developer-only TypeScript/Python schema tooling.

Use the agreed private/public distribution channel only. An immutable packed tarball with integrity is sufficient for the initial candidate; npm registry publication is not assumed. Never depend on a local file: path, moving main branch or source symlink for the delivered artifact.
Align docs with supported API/CLI and #75 service consumers.
**Expected surfaces:** package.json/lock/build config, public entry points, bin launcher, runtime asset packaging, pack/release scripts, API/CLI/install documentation.
outOfScope: No general driver reimplementation, live consumer migration, unapproved registry publication or mass dependency upgrade.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: An independent JS and TypeScript consumer imports only documented paths, including declarations, without development/source-tree dependencies.
AC-02: The installed CLI runs via the supported local/standalone invocation on Windows and POSIX; existing compatibility behavior is tested.
AC-03: Pack contents include every required asset and exclude secrets, .agent data, source-project history and unnecessary fixtures.
AC-04: Artifact identity and integrity are recorded; clean installation does not run workflows or overwrite project files.
AC-05: Missing runtime dependencies and unsupported package/API versions produce actionable errors.
AC-06: Distribution identity, rights/license and channel decisions from MIG-002 are satisfied before release.
validationPlan:
npm pack then install into a fresh external directory; compile an external TypeScript consumer and run JS imports, CLI help/version and configured primitive operations. Inspect the tarball allowlist and verify execution from a different cwd with the source checkout unavailable.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
